title: 50 mM Phosphate Buffer (with 0.02% sodium azide option)
author: Allen Institute for Brain Science
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bg52jy8e
materials: PF0315 TissueCyte Specimen Embedding Acrylamide Coembedding
Warning: Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) should be used at all times while operating this protocol. If you are unsure what PPE you should be using, see your immediate supervisor.
Ready to use 50 mM Phosphate Buffer
Solution can be stored at room temperature.
Clean area and dispose of used or excess reagents as appropriate.

steps.title: Calibrate equipment
steps.instruction: Calibrate the pH meter and the analytical balance before starting any preparation.

steps.title: Measure and prepare water
steps.instruction: Measure the required volume of Milli‑Q water for the desired final buffer volume, place it in an appropriately sized container (e.g., 1 L bottle, carboy, etc.), and add a clean stir bar.

substeps.instruction: For 1 L, 2 L, or 5 L preparations: use 1000 mL, 2000 mL, or 5000 mL of water respectively (or the reduced volumes shown in the tables when adding sodium azide).
For large‑volume preparations (10 L, 15 L, 20 L): use 800 mL, 1600 mL, or 4000 mL of water respectively before adjusting to final volume.

steps.title: Place on stir plate
steps.instruction: Put the container on a stir plate and set the speed to a medium setting (≥ 5).

steps.title: Add phosphate salts (and azide if required)
steps.instruction: Add sodium phosphate monobasic monohydrate (NaH₂PO₄·H₂O) and sodium phosphate dibasic anhydrous (Na₂HPO₄) to achieve a final concentration of 50 mM; if a sodium‑azide‑containing buffer is needed, add 5 % sodium azide stock to reach 0.02 % azide.

substeps.instruction: For 1 L final volume (no azide): add 0.66 g NaH₂PO₄·H₂O and 2.88 g Na₂HPO₄.
For 2 L final volume (no azide): add 1.32 g NaH₂PO₄·H₂O and 5.76 g Na₂HPO₄.
For 5 L final volume (no azide): add 3.30 g NaH₂PO₄·H₂O and 14.40 g Na₂HPO₄.
For 1 L buffer with 0.02 % azide: use 980 mL water, add 0.66 g NaH₂PO₄·H₂O, 2.88 g Na₂HPO₄, and 4 mL of 5 % sodium azide.
For 2 L buffer with 0.02 % azide: use 1960 mL water, add 1.32 g NaH₂PO₄·H₂O, 5.76 g Na₂HPO₄, and 8 mL of 5 % sodium azide.
For 5 L buffer with 0.02 % azide: use 4900 mL water, add 3.30 g NaH₂PO₄·H₂O, 14.40 g Na₂HPO₄, and 20 mL of 5 % sodium azide.

For 10 L, 15 L, or 20 L preparations (using 20× stock): add 13.2 g, 26.4 g, or 66 g NaH₂PO₄·H₂O respectively; add 57.6 g, 115.2 g, or 288 g Na₂HPO₄ respectively; add 40 mL, 60 mL, or 80 mL of 5 % sodium azide respectively; then adjust to the final volume with Milli‑Q water (9 L, 14 L, or 18 L).

steps.title: Stir until clear
steps.instruction: Stir the solution at medium speed (setting 5 or above) until it becomes clear.

steps.title: Adjust pH to 7.40
steps.instruction: Using the calibrated pH meter, adjust the solution pH to 7.40 (add acid or base as needed).

steps.title: Filter solution
steps.instruction: Set up a funnel with a piece of coarse filter paper and filter the buffer into clean 1‑L bottle(s).

steps.title: Label containers
steps.instruction: Label each bottle with the preparer’s initials, contents (50 mM phosphate buffer ± 0.02 % sodium azide), pH, and date of preparation.

steps.title: Degas buffer
steps.instruction: Degas the buffer according to SOP RP0017 until no air bubbles are observed; minimum time is 1 hour per liter (2 hours for 2 L).

steps.title: Store solution
steps.instruction: Store the degassed buffer at room temperature; it remains usable for up to 2 weeks. Note that sodium azide is highly toxic—handle with appropriate PPE and report any exposure.

steps.title: Prepare large‑volume buffer (optional)
steps.instruction: For final volumes greater than 5 L, first prepare a 20× (1 M) phosphate‑buffer stock, then dilute to the desired volume while adding sodium azide as described above.

substeps.instruction: Place a carboy on a stir plate, add a clean stir bar, and add the required volume of Milli‑Q water (e.g., 500 mL for 10 L final volume).
Add the appropriate amounts of NaH₂PO₄·H₂O, Na₂HPO₄, and 5 % sodium azide listed for the target final volume.
Stir at medium speed for 30 minutes.
Adjust pH to 7.40 with a calibrated pH meter.
Label the carboy or downstream bottles as above.
Degas the solution per SOP RP0017 (minimum 1 hour per liter).
Adjust to the final volume by adding Milli‑Q water (e.g., add 9 L water to reach 10 L total).
